verbose.description: If true, log extra debugging information during recovery.

output_dir.description: Absolute path to the directory where recovered files will be written.

log_file.description: Path to the log file where recovery activity (e.g., found files, errors) will be recorded.

max_file_size.description: Maximum size (in bytes) of recovered files. Set to 0 for unlimited size.

device_path.description: Block device or forensic image path (e.g., /dev/sdb, evidence.img) to scan for recoverable files.

file_types.description: List of file signatures to detect and recover. Each entry defines the file extension, header offset, hex magic bytes, and optional description.

offset.description: Byte offset where the magic signature must appear (usually 0)

magic.description: Hex string of the file header signature (e.g., 'ffd8ff' for JPEG)

block_size.description: Block size (in bytes) to read per I/O pass. Smaller values reduce memory use and are safer on damaged media.

subdirs.description: If true, organize recovered files into subdirectories named by extension (e.g., /output/jpg/). If false, all files go directly into the output directory.

overwrite.description: If true, overwrite existing files in the output directory (⚠️ use with caution — can destroy forensic integrity).

max_files.description: Maximum number of files to recover. Set to 0 to recover all possible files.

start_offsets.description: List of hex offsets (as strings) to begin scanning for signatures (e.g., ['0', '4096']). Often left at ['0'] for full-device scanning.

tz_offset.description: Timezone offset (in hours) to apply to timestamps in logs (e.g., -5 for EST).

case_sensitive.description: Legacy setting — if set to 'on', treats extensions as case-sensitive. Usually ignored in modern foremost versions.
